doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Deaths of Bucky and Ruth Pizzarelli and other musicians
summary: Reflection on the March obituaries, especially Bucky Pizzarelli, his family unable to be with him, and her driving him to Hamilton.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: There was a week, I believe near the end of March, where it seemed like every other day there was an obit.
That’s right. Bucky Pizzarelli and Ruth Pizzarelli, and Wallace Roney and many others.
And it just seemed like whoa, why is this hitting these older musicians with such regularity. And I remember thinking well Bucky was not in great health. We had almost lost him a couple of years ago.
Somehow it just didn’t seem fair that this took him.

It wasn’t fair at all, no. I agree, the saddest thing of all, I get chills thinking about it now, that John and Martin and Mary and the whole family — I don’t know for sure but this disease was so awful that you couldn’t be around your loved ones. That is just — I can’t even fathom that. I can’t fathom that. And of course Ruth going a week later you know. That’s the saddest thing of all. It isn’t fair you know what I mean? I mean he was such a survivor and such a wonderful guy. And I used to love driving him up to Hamilton, I just used to love chatting with him.
Yes. We treasure those moments maybe more than we did.
That’s right, of course. Absolutely. Yeah. Special guy.
